pages.text: Faisal loves football, but he is the smallest boy in his class. At break time, nobody picks him for a team.
"You're too small," says Omar. Faisal sits on a bench and watches the game. He is sad, but he doesn't go home.
On Thursday, there is a big match against another school. But Majed, the goalkeeper, is ill. "Who can catch the ball?" asks the teacher.
Faisal puts up his hand. "I can! I catch my brother's ball every day in the garden." Omar laughs, but the teacher says, "OK, Faisal. Get your gloves!"
The score is one-one. In the last minute, a tall boy kicks the ball very hard. Faisal jumps high and catches it!
Everyone shouts and claps. Omar runs to him and says, "Sorry, Faisal. You're small, but you're the best!" Faisal smiles. "Can I play with you at break time tomorrow?" "Of course!" says Omar.

questions.q: Why does nobody pick Faisal for a team?
Who is the goalkeeper before the big match?
Where does Faisal catch his brother's ball every day?
In the story, what does "ill" mean?
How does Omar feel at the end of the story?

pages.text: Layla and her grandpa made a robot. Its name was Tiko. Tiko had big round eyes, and they could shine like lamps.
"Tiko can't run or jump," said Layla's brother, Faisal. "He's very slow!" Tiko moved his arms and said, "Beep. I am sorry."
On Thursday, they took Tiko to the school science fair. There were robots that could dance, sing and play football. Layla felt sad.
Then suddenly, all the lights went out. It was very dark, and a little boy started to cry. "Where's my mum?" he shouted.
"Tiko, eyes on!" said Layla. Tiko's eyes shone bright yellow, and slowly he walked to the boy. Now everyone could see, and the boy found his mum.
The teacher gave Tiko a gold star. Faisal smiled. "Slow is OK. Tiko is the best robot here!"

questions.q: Who made Tiko with Layla?
What can Tiko's eyes do?
What does "dark" mean in the story?
options: There is a lot of light
There is a lot of noise

questions.q: Why did Layla feel sad at the science fair?
options: The other robots could do more things

questions.q: How did Faisal feel about Tiko at the end?
options: He still thought Tiko was bad

pages.text: Faisal and his grandmother walked in old Jeddah. The houses were tall and very old. "This street is two hundred years old," Grandma said.
Grandma stopped at a big green door. She took an old key out of her bag. "I lived here when I was a girl," she said.
The key was heavy, and the door opened slowly. Inside, it was dark and quiet. Faisal saw beautiful wooden windows.
"Where did you sleep, Grandma?" asked Faisal. "Up those stairs," she said. "Come, I want to show you something."
In a small room, Grandma touched the wall. There were old letters on it: "Huda, 10 years old." "I wrote that sixty years ago!" she laughed.
Faisal took a small stone from the floor. He wrote under her name: "Faisal, 9 years old." "Now this house has our story too," Grandma said with a smile.

questions.q: Where did Faisal and his grandmother walk?
What color was the big door?
What does "heavy" mean in the story?
Who wrote "Huda, 10 years old" on the wall?
options: Grandma when she was a girl

questions.q: Why did Grandma say, "Now this house has our story too"?
options: Because both their names were now on the wall
Because Faisal found a new key

pages.text: Omar and his family went to the beach by the Red Sea. At night, the moon was big and white. "Look! Something is moving in the sand!" said his sister, Lina.
They were baby turtles! They were very small and had tiny flippers. But the turtles walked away from the sea.
"Why are they going the wrong way?" asked Omar. Dad pointed to the bright lights of the café. "They think the lights are the moon on the water," he said.
Omar ran to the café. "Please turn off the lights for ten minutes!" he said. The man smiled and turned them off.
Now the beach was dark, and the moon shone on the sea. The baby turtles turned around. They walked quickly to the water.
One small turtle stopped and looked back. "Goodbye, little friend!" said Lina. Then a wave came, and the turtle swam away into the big, blue sea.

questions.q: Where did Omar and his family go?
options: To the beach by the Red Sea
To a park in the city
To a farm in the desert

questions.q: Why did the baby turtles walk the wrong way?
options: They thought the café lights were the moon on the water
They wanted to play with Lina

questions.q: What does "tiny" mean?
What did Omar ask the man at the café to do?
How do you think Omar and Lina felt at the end?

pages.text: Every Friday, Grandma makes date cakes, and they are the best cakes in the family. "What's your secret, Grandma?" asks Lina.
Grandma smiles and holds up a small blue box. "My secret is in here," she says, but she never opens it.
One Friday, Grandma is sick in bed, and the cousins are coming for lunch. "Oh no! No date cakes today!" cries Omar, but Lina says, "Don't worry, I can make them!"
Lina mixes flour, butter, eggs and dates, and she bakes the cakes in the oven. They look beautiful, but they taste wrong. Something is missing!
Lina runs to Grandma's room, and Grandma gives her the blue box. Inside, there is a brown powder with a wonderful smell. "It's cardamom, just one small spoon!" says Grandma.
Lina makes the cakes again, and the family eats every one. "These are Grandma's cakes!" says Omar. Grandma laughs and says, "No, now they are Lina's cakes."

questions.q: When does Grandma make date cakes?
Why can't Grandma make the cakes this Friday?
What is in the blue box?
In the story, "bakes" means:
Why does Grandma say, "Now they are Lina's cakes"?
options: Because Lina ate all the cakes
Because Lina can make the cakes well now, and the secret is hers too
Because Grandma doesn't like the cakes

pages.text: Lina loved music. Every morning, she sang in the garden with the birds. "One day, I want to play in a concert," she said.
"Next week, we have a school concert," said her teacher. "Bring an instrument!" But Lina didn't have a drum or a guitar, and she felt sad.
At home, Grandpa hit his glass with a spoon. Ding! "Listen, Lina," he said. "Water can sing too!"
They put seven bottles on the table. Some bottles had a lot of water, and some had a little. Each bottle made a different sound.
Lina practised every evening after her homework. Her little brother danced and laughed. Soon she could play a whole song.
At the concert, everyone looked at the bottles and smiled. Then Lina played, and the room was very quiet. At the end, everyone clapped, and Grandpa clapped the loudest!

questions.q: What did Lina NOT have for the concert?
Who gave Lina the idea to use water?
"The room was very quiet." What does "quiet" mean?
Why did each bottle make a different sound?
options: The bottles had different amounts of water

questions.q: How did Grandpa probably feel at the end?

stories.title: The Case of the Missing Hat

pages.text: "Where is my white hat?" asked Grandpa at the desert camp. "It was on this chair!" Sara and Omar took out their notebook and said, "Don't worry, Grandpa. We are detectives!"
Next to the chair, Omar saw big round footprints in the sand. "Look! These are not people's feet," he said. "They are very, very big!"
Then Sara found small pieces of dry grass on the chair. "Who eats grass?" she asked. "Goats eat grass," said Omar, and he wrote it in the notebook.
They followed the footprints behind the big tent. The goats were asleep there, and their feet were very small. "It isn't the goats," said Sara. "The footprints don't stop here!"
Then they heard a funny noise behind a palm tree. It was Noura, Grandpa's camel! She had the white hat on her head, and she looked very happy.
Everyone laughed, and Grandpa laughed the loudest. "Case closed!" said Sara. Grandpa gave his two clever detectives sweet dates and a big hug.

questions.q: Where was Grandpa's hat at the start?
What did Sara find on the chair?
Why did Sara say, "It isn't the goats"?
options: The goats were in the tent

questions.q: What does "footprints" mean?
How did Grandpa feel at the end?

pages.text: Faisal loves superheroes, and he draws them every day in his big blue book. "I want a superpower too!" he says to his grandpa.
Grandpa smiles. "You have one, Faisal. You see small things that other people don't see." Faisal laughs. "That's not a superpower, Grandpa!"
On Friday, Faisal and Grandpa go to the park. Faisal hears a little boy crying under a tree. "I can't find my mum," says the boy. "She has a yellow bag."
Faisal looks and looks. There are many people and many bags in the park. Then he sees something yellow behind the tall trees, next to the shop.
A woman with a yellow bag is calling, "Yusuf! Yusuf!" The little boy runs to his mum, and she hugs him. "Thank you, Faisal!" she says.
That night, Faisal opens his blue book and draws a new superhero with very big eyes. He writes a name under it: SUPER EYES. Grandpa smiles. "Now you know your superpower!"

questions.q: What does Faisal draw in his blue book?
What colour is the mum's bag?
Where is the little boy crying?
What does "hugs" mean in the story?
options: Puts arms around someone with love

questions.q: Why is Grandpa right about Faisal's superpower?
options: Faisal sees small things and finds the boy's mum

pages.text: Omar and his family went camping in the desert. Dad put up a big tent near the rocks. Omar's sister, Huda, carried the blankets.
At night, they sat by the fire and ate dates. "Look at the stars!" said Huda. "There are hundreds!"
Later, Omar heard a sound outside the tent. Scratch, scratch! "What's that?" whispered Huda.
Omar took his torch and looked outside. Something small and round was next to the bag of dates. It was brown, and it had lots of sharp spikes!
"It's a hedgehog!" laughed Omar. "It's hungry, like us." Huda put a date on a rock for it.
In the morning, the date wasn't there. Next to the rock, there were tiny footprints in the sand. "Our first camping friend!" Dad said with a smile.

questions.q: Where did Omar's family go camping?
What did the family eat by the fire?
What did Omar use to look outside at night?
What does "whispered" mean?
Why wasn't the date on the rock in the morning?

pages.text: On Sunday morning, Omar ran into his classroom. The class tortoise, Speedy, lived in a big box by the window. But today, the box was empty!
"Where is Speedy?" Omar shouted. Mr. Khalid looked under every desk. "Tortoises are very slow, so he can't be far," he said.
The boys looked in the library and in the playground. Faisal checked behind the big bookcase. But they couldn't find Speedy anywhere.
Back in the classroom, Omar heard a quiet sound: crunch, crunch, crunch! It came from Yusuf's school bag. The bag was on the floor next to Speedy's box.
Yusuf opened his bag slowly. There was Speedy, eating Yusuf's lettuce sandwich! Everyone laughed, and Yusuf laughed the loudest.
"Speedy isn't slow when he is hungry!" said Mr. Khalid. That afternoon, the class made a strong new lid for the box. Now Yusuf brings an extra piece of lettuce every day, just for Speedy.

questions.q: Where did Speedy live?
options: In a big box by the window

questions.q: Where did Faisal look for Speedy?
What does "empty" mean in the story?
How did Omar find Speedy?
options: He saw him in the playground

questions.q: Why did the class make a new lid for the box?
options: So Speedy can't get out again
Because the old box was too small
Because Speedy didn't like the window

pages.text: On Friday, my family went to the desert. Dad put up a big tent, and Mum made hot tea. My little brother Fahad played in the sand.
Then Grandma looked around. "Where is Fahad?" she asked. We called his name, but there was no answer.
Dad took his torch, and I held Grandma's hand. We walked up a big hill of sand. The wind was cold, and the sun went down.
Then I saw small footprints in the sand. "Look, Dad! Fahad went this way!" I shouted. We followed them quickly.
Behind a tree, we found Fahad. He was next to a mother camel and her baby! "The baby is hungry," Fahad said, and he gave it his bread.
Dad laughed and picked Fahad up. "Next time, you must stay with your family," Grandma said with a smile. Back at the tent, we all drank tea under the bright stars.

questions.q: Where did the family go on Friday?
Who first asked, "Where is Fahad?"
What are "footprints"?
options: Marks from feet in the sand

questions.q: Why did Fahad give his bread to the baby camel?
options: Dad told him to do it

questions.q: How did the family probably feel at the end of the story?

pages.text: Sara has a small robot. Its name is Zoom. Zoom is round, and it cleans the floor every morning.
One day, Grandma was sad. "I can't find my gold ring!" she said. Everyone looked under the chairs and tables.
Sara had an idea. "Zoom has a camera," she said. "It can go under the sofa!"
Zoom went under the big sofa. Sara watched on her tablet. It was very dark, but then something was shining.
"Stop, Zoom!" Sara shouted. Dad moved the sofa. There was Grandma's ring, next to an old toy car!
Grandma smiled and hugged Sara. "Thank you, clever girl! And thank you, Zoom!" Zoom beeped happily.

questions.q: What does Zoom do every morning?
What did Grandma lose?
How did Sara see under the sofa?
options: She watched Zoom's camera on her tablet.

questions.q: In the story, "shining" means:
Why did Grandma call Sara "clever"?
options: Because Sara had a good idea to find the ring.
Because Sara found a toy car.

stories.title: The Man in the Dark Room

pages.text: A long time ago, a clever man lived in Cairo. His name was Ibn al-Haytham. He loved light, and he asked many questions.
"How do our eyes see?" he asked his young helper, Yusuf. "Light comes from the sun," said Yusuf. "Yes, but how does it go into our eyes?"
Ibn al-Haytham went into a very dark room. There was one small hole in the wall. "Come and look, Yusuf!" he called.
On the wall, there was a picture of the street outside! Yusuf saw a camel and a tree. "But the camel is upside down!" he laughed.
"Light moves in straight lines," said Ibn al-Haytham. "It comes through the hole and makes a picture. Our eyes work like this room."
Yusuf smiled. "You are a hero of light!" Ibn al-Haytham wrote many books about light. Today, every camera works like his dark room.

questions.q: Where did Ibn al-Haytham live?
What was in the wall of the dark room?
What does "upside down" mean?
options: With the top at the bottom

questions.q: Why did Yusuf laugh?
options: The camel was upside down in the picture

questions.q: Why is Ibn al-Haytham a hero today?
options: He was a very fast runner
He helped people understand light and how we see

pages.text: It is a hot day in the desert. Omar and his sister Lina are at Grandpa's farm. The sky is blue, and the sun is very strong.
Suddenly, Lina points. "Look, Omar! The sky is orange!" A big wall of sand is coming fast.
"It's a sandstorm!" says Grandpa. "Quick! Bring the goats into the barn!" Omar runs to the goats, and Lina closes the gate.
Now they are in the house. The wind is loud, and the windows are shaking. Omar counts the goats in his head. "Oh no! The baby goat is missing!"
Then they hear a small sound. "Baa!" The baby goat is under the kitchen table! "He is scared of the wind too," says Lina, and everyone laughs.
After an hour, the wind stops. Then it starts to rain! Grandpa smiles. "First sand, then rain. That is desert weather!"

questions.q: Where are Omar and Lina?
What color is the sky when the sandstorm comes?
Where is the baby goat?
What does "scared" mean in the story?
Why does the baby goat go into the house?
options: It wants to play with Lina
It wants to hide from the wind

pages.text: Omar loved painting. On Sunday, there was an art competition at his school. He wanted to paint the desert.
He painted yellow sand and a big blue sky. Then he added a brown camel. "It's finished!" he said.
His little sister Huda ran into the room. Oh no! She dropped a cup of water on the painting.
The red, yellow and blue paint ran together. Omar was very sad. "My picture is wrong now!" he cried.
Huda looked at the painting carefully. "Look, Omar! The sky is orange and pink now. It's an evening sky!"
At school, the teacher smiled. "What a beautiful sunset!" she said. Omar won first prize, and he hugged Huda. "Thank you! You're an artist too!"

questions.q: What did Omar want to paint?
What animal did Omar add to his painting?
What did Huda drop on the painting?
What does "sunset" mean in the story?
options: The sky at night with stars
The sky in the evening when the sun goes down

questions.q: Why did Omar say, "You're an artist too!" to Huda?
options: Because her water made his sky beautiful
Because she won a prize at school

pages.text: Noor found an old clock in Grandpa's room. It had a small gold key. She turned the key, and the room went round and round!
Now Noor was in a village with no cars. A boy sat next to a little house. "I want a tree, but I have only one seed," he said.
"Let's plant it together!" said Noor. They dug a hole and gave the seed some water. "Thank you! My name is Saad," said the boy.
Then the clock went tick, tick, tick. Noor waved goodbye to Saad. The room went round and round again.
Noor ran outside to Grandpa Saad. There was a big palm tree in the garden. "I planted this tree with a girl a long time ago," Grandpa said.
"She had a clock like yours," he laughed. Noor smiled and gave him a sweet date from the tree. "Thank you, my old friend," she said.

questions.q: What did Noor find in Grandpa's room?
What did the boy want?
What does "dug" mean in the story?
options: They made a hole in the ground

questions.q: Who is the boy Saad?
Why did Grandpa laugh at the end?
options: Because the date was not sweet
Because he knew Noor was the girl from long ago

pages.text: Faisal and his sister Noura went to the beach in Jeddah with Dad. The sea was blue and the sand was hot. But there was a lot of rubbish on the sand.
"Look!" shouted Noura. "Something is moving in that plastic bag!" They ran to it quickly.
It was a small sea turtle. It couldn't swim because the bag was around its leg. "Be careful," said Dad.
Faisal held the turtle gently. Noura took the bag off its leg. The turtle opened its eyes and looked at them.
They put the turtle near the water. It walked slowly into the waves and swam away. "Goodbye, little friend!" Noura laughed.
Then Faisal had an idea. "Let's clean the beach for all the turtles!" They picked up bottles and bags all afternoon, and Dad was very proud.

questions.q: Where did Faisal and Noura go?
Why couldn't the turtle swim?
options: The bag was around its leg

questions.q: What does "gently" mean?
options: In a soft and careful way

questions.q: What did the children pick up in the afternoon?
Why was Dad proud at the end?
options: Because the children helped the beach and the animals
Because the children swam very far
Because the children found a new toy

pages.text: Every morning, Mr. Saleh stood at the school gate. He smiled and said, "Good morning!" to every student. But there was no shade, and the sun was very hot.
One day, Huda saw Mr. Saleh's red face. "He's hot and tired," she said to her friend Noura. "Let's help him!"
At break time, the girls told their teacher, Miss Amal. "What a good idea!" she said. "The whole class can help."
The next day, everyone brought something. Huda brought a big green umbrella, and Noura brought a cold bottle of water. The other girls made a card with a picture of a smiling sun.
In the morning, the class ran to the gate. "Surprise!" they shouted. Mr. Saleh opened the card, and his eyes were wet with happy tears.
"Thank you, my daughters," he said. On Thursday, he brought a big box of sweet dates for the whole class. "Kindness is like a ball," Huda laughed. "When you throw it, it comes back to you!"

questions.q: Where did Mr. Saleh stand every morning?
Why did Huda want to help Mr. Saleh?
What did Huda bring?
What does "shade" mean in the story?
options: A cool place out of the sun

questions.q: Why did Mr. Saleh bring dates on Thursday?
options: He wanted to say thank you to the class

pages.text: Omar and his grandfather camped in the desert. At night, Omar went to say goodnight to Nour, the baby camel. But Nour was not there!
"Grandpa, Nour is lost!" Omar shouted. Grandpa took his torch, and Omar took a bottle of water. "Come on, let's find her," said Grandpa.
They followed small footprints in the sand. Then the wind blew hard, and the footprints were gone. "What can we do now?" Omar asked quietly.
Grandpa looked up at the sky. "Look at that bright star. Camels often walk to the old rocks under it."
They walked to a big hill with old rocks. Omar heard a sad, soft sound behind a rock. It was Nour, and her leg was stuck between two stones!
Omar moved the stones carefully, and Nour stood up. Omar gave her some water, and they walked back to the tent. "You were very brave tonight," Grandpa said, and Omar smiled at the star.

questions.q: Who is Nour?
Why did the footprints go away?
What does "stuck" mean in the story?
Where did they find Nour?
options: Behind a rock on a big hill

questions.q: Why did Omar smile at the star at the end?
options: Because the star helped them find Nour

pages.text: Omar lives near the desert with his grandfather. They have ten camels. The smallest camel is Noor, and she loves Omar's whistle.
One afternoon, the wind was very strong. Sand flew everywhere, and everyone ran inside. "Where is Noor?" Omar shouted.
When the wind stopped, Omar and Grandpa looked for her. They looked behind the tents and next to the water. But Noor wasn't there.
"Camels can walk a long way," Grandpa said sadly. Then Omar had an idea. He climbed a tall sand hill and whistled loudly.
They waited and waited. Then they heard a quiet sound from behind the big rocks. Noor ran up the hill to Omar!
That night, Noor drank warm milk next to Omar. "You're a clever boy," Grandpa smiled. "No, Grandpa," Omar laughed. "Noor is the clever one. She listened!"

questions.q: How many camels do Omar and his grandfather have?
What happened one afternoon?
What does "quiet" mean in the story?
Where was Noor?
Why did Omar whistle on the hill?
options: Because Noor knows and loves his whistle

pages.text: Noor's aunt, Huda, is an astronaut. Tonight, she is far away in space. Noor wants to see her.
After dinner, Noor and Grandpa go up to the roof with a telescope. The sky is dark and full of stars.
"Look, Grandpa, that star is moving!" says Noor. Grandpa smiles and says, "It's not a star. It's the space station."
"Is Aunt Huda in there?" asks Noor. "Yes, she is," says Grandpa. Noor jumps up and waves.
The bright light goes across the sky, and then it is gone. Noor feels a little sad. "Can she see me?" she asks.
The next morning, Aunt Huda calls on the phone. "I saw the lights of your city last night," she says. "I waved to you, Noor!"

questions.q: What is Aunt Huda's job?
Where do Noor and Grandpa go after dinner?
What is the 'fast star' really?
What does 'bright' mean in the story?
How does Noor probably feel at the end of the story?
options: Happy, because Aunt Huda waved to her
Angry, because the light was gone

stories.title: The Slow Boy in the Goal

pages.text: Yusuf loves football, but he is not fast. In every game, the other boys run past him. "Never mind," says his grandfather. "Try something different."
On Friday, the school team has a big match. Their goalkeeper, Sami, is ill. "Who can stand in the goal?" asks Coach Khalid.
Nobody answers. Then Yusuf puts up his hand. "I can't run fast, but I can catch!" he says.
The match starts. The other team kicks the ball again and again. Yusuf jumps and catches it every time.
It is the last minute, and the score is one-one. A tall boy kicks the ball very hard. Yusuf flies to the left and stops it!
Then Yusuf throws the ball far to Ali, and Ali scores. Everyone shouts, "Yusuf! Yusuf!" Now he has a new place on the team.

questions.q: What is Yusuf's problem at the start?
Why does the team need a new goalkeeper?
What does "catch" mean in the story?
options: To take the ball in your hands

questions.q: What happens in the last minute?
How does Yusuf feel at the end?

pages.text: Mum's silver ring was on the kitchen table. In the morning, it wasn't there! "Where is my ring?" Mum asked.
The next day, Dad's car key went missing. Then Omar's new spoon went too. "Who is taking our shiny things?" said Omar.
Omar and his sister Lina looked for clues. They found a small black feather by the open window. "A feather!" said Lina.
The children waited quietly near the window. Suddenly, a black bird flew into the kitchen! It took a shiny button and flew to the palm tree.
Dad got a ladder and climbed up the tree. In the bird's nest, he found the ring, the key and the spoon! "Here is our thief," he laughed.
Mum was very happy to have her ring again. Lina put an old shiny button in the nest. "That's for you, Mr Bird!" she said.

questions.q: What did Mum lose first?
What did the children find by the window?
What does "suddenly" mean in the story?
options: Very quickly, and nobody thinks it will happen

questions.q: Where was the bird's nest?
Why did the bird take the things?

pages.text: Yusuf and Adam were at the beach in Jeddah. They wanted to build the biggest sandcastle in the world. "Let's start!" said Adam.
Yusuf made a tall tower, and Adam made a long wall. "My tower is the best!" said Yusuf. "No, my wall is better!" shouted Adam.
The boys stopped talking. Yusuf sat on one side, and Adam sat on the other side. Then Adam saw a very big wave.
"Yusuf, quick! Help me!" Adam called. They put sand on the wall together, fast, fast, fast! But the water came over the wall.
The tower fell down into the water. The boys looked at each other. Then they laughed and laughed.
"Let's build it again," said Yusuf. "Together this time!" At sunset, their castle was the biggest on the beach.

questions.q: Where were Yusuf and Adam?
What did Yusuf make first?
What is a "wave"?
options: Water that moves in the sea

questions.q: Why did the boys stop talking?
options: They were angry with each other

questions.q: What did the boys learn at the end?
options: It is better to build together

stories.title: The Magic of the Sun Plate

pages.text: Omar washed the yard with Grandpa. There was a big puddle near the door. After lunch, the puddle was gone!
"Where did the water go?" asked Omar. Grandpa smiled. "Let's do a test and find out."
Grandpa put salty water on two plates. One plate went in the hot sun. The other plate went in the dark kitchen.
Omar checked the plates every hour. The sun plate got drier and drier. The kitchen plate was still wet.
In the evening, the sun plate had no water, but there was white salt on it! "The sun took the water up into the air," said Grandpa.
"The water goes up, but the salt stays!" said Omar. That night, Mum put Omar's salt on the salad. "Science tastes good!" Omar laughed.

questions.q: Where was the big puddle?
Where did Grandpa put the second plate?
What does "wet" mean in the story?
What was on the sun plate in the evening?
Why was the kitchen plate still wet?
options: Because there was no hot sun there
Because Omar put more water on it

pages.text: Faisal and his grandpa drove into the desert. They wanted to see the stars. The sand was gold, and the sky was very big.
At night, the car stopped. "Grandpa, the car is broken!" said Faisal. His phone didn't work, too.
Grandpa smiled. "Don't be afraid. The stars can help us." He pointed to a very bright star.
"That star shows us the north. Our camp is north," said Grandpa. They walked slowly over the cold sand.
Then Faisal heard a sound. It was a camel! Behind it, he saw a small fire and a tent.
"You found us!" shouted Uncle Khalid. They drank hot milk by the fire. Faisal looked up and said quietly, "Thank you, stars."

questions.q: Why did Faisal and Grandpa go into the desert?
What happened to the car at night?
What does "afraid" mean?
How did Grandpa know the way to the camp?
options: He looked at a bright star

questions.q: How did Faisal feel at the end of the story?

pages.text: Omar has a green parrot. Her name is Kiwi. Kiwi is very clever and can say lots of words.
One afternoon, Kiwi shouted, "Dinner is ready!" Dad ran to the kitchen. Omar and his sister ran too.
But the table was empty. Mum laughed and said, "I didn't say that. Kiwi did!"
The next day, Kiwi shouted, "Omar! Do your homework!" Omar sat down and opened his book. Then he saw Kiwi's funny face and laughed.
In the evening, Mum called, "Dinner is ready!" Nobody came. "It's Kiwi again," Dad said with a smile.
Then Kiwi shouted, "I'm hungry! Come quickly!" Everyone ran to the kitchen. This time there was hot rice and chicken, and Kiwi got a big piece of mango!

pages.text: Noura and her grandfather went out on his small boat. The Red Sea was blue and quiet. 'Look for dolphins!' Grandpa said.
Suddenly, Noura saw something in the water. It was a big sea turtle. It couldn't swim because an old fishing net was around its legs.
'Grandpa, help!' Noura shouted. Grandpa stopped the boat. He took his small knife and moved slowly to the turtle.
'Be careful!' said Noura. Grandpa cut the net, piece by piece. The turtle was tired, but it moved its legs again.
The turtle swam around the boat one time. Then it looked at Noura with its dark eyes. 'It's saying thank you!' she laughed.
Noura put the old net in a bag. 'Now it can't hurt more animals,' she said. Just then, two dolphins jumped next to the boat, and Grandpa smiled.

questions.q: Where were Noura and her grandfather?
options: On a boat on the Red Sea
On a beach in the desert
In a big ship in the city

questions.q: Why couldn't the turtle swim?
options: A fishing net was around its legs

questions.q: What did Grandpa use to help the turtle?
In the story, 'tired' means:
Why did Noura put the old net in a bag?
options: She wanted to catch fish with it
She wanted to give it to Grandpa
She didn't want it to hurt more sea animals

pages.text: Noura loves building things. Her grandpa has a small garden with tomatoes. Every day, he carries heavy water to the plants.
"My back hurts," Grandpa said one hot morning. Noura looked at the old plastic bottles in the kitchen. "I have an idea!" she said.
Mum helped her make small holes in the bottles. Then Noura filled them with water. She put them upside down in the ground next to the plants.
Her brother Fahad laughed. "Bottles can't water plants!" But the next morning, the ground was wet and the leaves were green.
Grandpa smiled. "The water comes out slowly, drop by drop," he said. "You made rain under the ground!"
Now Grandpa sits under the palm tree and drinks his tea. Fahad wants to be an inventor too. "My next idea is a robot for my homework!" he says.

questions.q: What does Grandpa carry every day?
Who helped Noura make holes in the bottles?
In the story, what does "wet" mean?
Why did Noura make her invention?
options: She wanted to make Fahad laugh

questions.q: How does Fahad feel about inventions at the end?
options: He wants to make one too

pages.text: Grandpa showed Omar an old photo. "This is me at Elephant Rock. I was ten." Omar said, "I'm ten too! Can we go there?"
The family drove to AlUla. The desert was big and orange. Omar looked out of the window all day.
At night, they slept in a tent. The sky was full of stars. "Tomorrow we find the elephant," Grandpa said.
In the morning, they walked between tall rocks. "Is that the elephant?" asked Omar's sister, Lina. "No!" laughed Omar. "That rock looks like a camel!"
Then Omar saw a giant rock with a long nose. "There it is!" he shouted. Grandpa smiled. "It's bigger than I remember."
Omar stood in the same place as Grandpa in the old photo. Dad took a new photo. Now the family had two photos: Grandpa at ten and Omar at ten.

questions.q: How old was Grandpa in the old photo?
Where did the family sleep at night?
What did the first rock look like?
What does "giant" mean in the story?
Why was the new photo special?
options: Omar was ten, like Grandpa in the old photo

words.ex: I get up at seven o'clock.

dialogue.t: What time do you get up?
I get up at six o'clock. What about you?
I get up at seven o'clock. Then I wash my face.
Do you brush your teeth before breakfast?
No, I brush my teeth after breakfast.
Me too! Then I get dressed and go to school by car.
I go to school by bus. My bus comes at half past seven.

grammar.title: Present simple for daily routines
grammar.ar: نستخدم المضارع البسيط للحديث عن الأشياء التي نفعلها كل يوم، مثل: I get up. نستخدم at مع الساعة: at seven o'clock. ونستخدم before بمعنى «قبل» و after بمعنى «بعد». وللسؤال عن الوقت نقول: What time do you ...?
examples: I get up at seven o'clock.
I have breakfast before school.
What time do you go to school?

words.ex: Look at my school timetable.
My favourite subject is Art.
On Sunday I have Maths.
Science is interesting because we do experiments.
We play football in PE.
I love Art because I can draw pictures.

dialogue.t: Hi! What lessons do you have on Sunday?
On Sunday I have Maths, English and Science.
Do you have PE on Monday?
Yes, I do. We play football. Do you have Art on Monday?
No, I don't. I have Art on Tuesday.
What's your favourite subject?
My favourite subject is Science because it's interesting.
My favourite subject is PE because it's fun!

grammar.title: Do you have ...? Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
grammar.ar: للسؤال بنعم أو لا في المضارع البسيط نضع Do في بداية الجملة: Do you have Maths? نجيب باختصار: Yes, I do أو No, I don't، ولا نكرر الفعل have في الإجابة. نستخدم on مع أيام الأسبوع: on Sunday.
examples: Do you have English on Sunday?
Yes, I do.
No, I don't. I have English on Monday.

words.ex: I always drink milk in the morning.
I usually walk to school.
I sometimes eat sweets.
I never drink cola.
She eats fruit every day.
Vegetables are healthy.

dialogue.t: How often do you eat fruit?
I always eat fruit. I love apples and bananas.
How often do you drink water?
I drink water every day.
Do you eat sweets?
Sometimes. But I never drink cola.
Great! Teacher, Ali always eats fruit. He drinks water every day and he never drinks cola.

grammar.title: Adverbs of frequency and he/she + -s
grammar.ar: كلمات التكرار مثل always و usually و sometimes و never تأتي قبل الفعل: I always eat fruit. للسؤال عن عدد المرات نقول: How often do you ...? وعندما نتحدث عن he أو she نضيف s إلى الفعل: He eats, She drinks.
examples: I usually go to bed at nine o'clock.
How often do you play outside?
She drinks milk every day.

words.ex: I do my homework after lunch.
I play football with my friends.
Can you ride your bike after school?
I watch TV for one hour.
I like reading books in the evening.

dialogue.t: What do you do after school?
After school I have lunch. First I do my homework, then I watch TV.
I don't like watching TV for a long time. I like playing football.
Can you play football after school today?
Yes, I can! First homework, then football at five o'clock.
Good idea. And then family time?
Yes. Then I have dinner with my family and read a book.

grammar.title: like / don't like + -ing
grammar.ar: بعد like و don't like نضيف ing إلى الفعل: I like playing، I don't like watching TV. نستخدم First ثم then لترتيب الأحداث: First I do my homework, then I play. ونستخدم Can you ...? لنسأل عن قدرة شخص أو لنطلب منه شيئًا.
examples: I like riding my bike.
First I eat lunch, then I do my homework.
Can you come to the park after school?

My mum cooks dinner. I help my mum with the salad.
Who washes the dishes?
My sister washes the dishes, and my brother takes out the rubbish.
In my house, my dad feeds the cat. I make my bed every day.
Look, Mum is busy. Mum, can I help you with the dishes?
That's kind! I can help too.

grammar.title: Who ...? and Can I help you with ...?
grammar.ar: نستخدم Who بمعنى «مَن» للسؤال عن الشخص الذي يقوم بالعمل، ويأخذ الفعل بعده s: Who cooks dinner? وعند الحديث عن my brother أو my sister نضيف s أيضًا: My sister washes. ولنعرض المساعدة بلطف نقول: Can I help you with ...?
examples: Who cleans the kitchen in your house?
My brother feeds the cat.
Can I help you with the shopping, Dad?

dialogue.t: Hello! This is my day. In the morning I get up at six o'clock and go to school.
In the afternoon I do my homework and play football.
In the evening I read a book and go to bed at nine o'clock.

Thank you! What's your favourite part of the day?
My favourite part is the afternoon because I play with my friends.
Who do you visit at the weekend?
I visit my grandma and grandpa. They live near the sea.

grammar.title: Time phrases: in the morning / at the weekend
grammar.ar: نستخدم in مع أجزاء اليوم: in the morning، in the afternoon، in the evening. لكن نستخدم at مع at the weekend و at night. ولنعبّر عن رأينا ونعطي السبب نقول: I think ... because ...
examples: In the evening I watch TV with my family.
At the weekend I go to the park.
I think my day is busy because I have a lot of homework.

dialogue.t: Hi! Welcome to my neighbourhood.
Thanks! Is there a park near your house?

Cool! Is there a library?
No, there isn't a library. But there are some shops. What's in your town?

Wow! I want to visit your town!

grammar.title: There is / There are
grammar.ar: نستخدم There is مع الاسم المفرد، ونستخدم There are مع الاسم الجمع، ومعناهما «يوجد / توجد». للسؤال نقدّم is فنقول: Is there a ...? وللنفي نقول: There isn't a .... كلمة some تعني «بعض»، وlots of تعني «الكثير من»، ونستخدمهما مع الجمع.
examples: There is a mosque near my house.
There are lots of shops in my town.
Is there a park in your town? No, there isn't.

words.ex: The bank is next to the school.

grammar.title: Prepositions of place
grammar.ar: حروف الجر المكانية تخبرنا أين يوجد الشيء، وتأتي بعد is وقبل the، مثل: next to (بجانب)، opposite (مقابل)، behind (خلف). كلمة between تحتاج إلى مكانين بينهما and. ومع أسماء الشوارع نستخدم on، مثل: It's on King Street.
examples: The library is next to the mosque.
The toy shop is between the café and the bank.

Go out of the mall and turn left.

Then go straight on and turn right at the traffic lights.
Right at the traffic lights?
Yes. The park is on your left. It's next to the mosque.
Thank you very much!
You're welcome!

grammar.title: Giving directions
grammar.ar: لإعطاء الاتجاهات نستخدم صيغة الأمر، فنبدأ الجملة بالفعل مباشرة بدون فاعل، مثل: Go و Turn. نستخدم at قبل المكان الذي ننعطف عنده، مثل: Turn left at the bank. ولكي نسأل عن الطريق بأدب نبدأ بـ Excuse me.
examples: Go straight on.
Turn right at the supermarket.
Excuse me, how do I get to the library?

grammar.title: How much is / How much are
grammar.ar: نستخدم How much is ...? للسؤال عن سعر شيء واحد، ونستخدم How much are ...? للسؤال عن سعر أشياء جمع أو كلمات تأتي دائمًا بصيغة الجمع مثل scissors. لطلب شيء بأدب نقول: Can I have ..., please? ونستخدم any في السؤال: Have you got any ...?

grammar.title: by + transport / walk to
grammar.ar: نستخدم by مع وسيلة المواصلات بدون a أو the، مثل: by car و by bus. أما عند المشي فنقول: I walk to ... ولا نقول by walk. وللسؤال عن طريقة الوصول نقول: How do you get to ...?

grammar.title: You can ... / It's got ... / because
grammar.ar: نستخدم You can + الفعل للتعبير عمّا يمكن فعله في مكان ما، ويبقى الفعل بعد can في صيغته الأصلية بدون إضافات. عبارة It's got تعني «فيه / لديه» وهي اختصار It has got. ونستخدم because لنذكر السبب، ومعناها «لأنّ».

grammar.title: Was and Were
grammar.ar: نستخدم was وwere للحديث عن الماضي، وهما الماضي من am وis وare. نستخدم was مع I وhe وshe وit، ونستخدم were مع you وwe وthey. للسؤال نضع was أو were قبل الفاعل، مثل: Where were you?
examples: I was at the mall on Friday.
We were at the beach on Saturday.
Where were you last weekend?

words.ex: On Saturday I played football with my brother.
We visited my aunt on Friday.

Did you visit your cousins?
Yes, I did. We visited them after that. Did you play football?
No, I didn't. I helped my mum at home.
Did you watch TV?
Yes, I did. I watched cartoons in the evening.

grammar.title: Past Simple: -ed Verbs and Did
grammar.ar: للحديث عن شيء حدث في الماضي نضيف ed إلى آخر كثير من الأفعال، مثل play تصبح played. عند السؤال نستخدم Did في البداية ويعود الفعل إلى أصله بدون ed. نجيب بـ Yes, I did أو No, I didn't.
examples: On Friday I visited my grandparents.
Did you watch the football match?
No, I didn't. I played with my sister.

words.ex: We were very happy at Eid.

What did you wear?

I wore new white clothes. It was a great Eid!

grammar.title: Irregular Past Verbs
grammar.ar: بعض الأفعال لا نضيف لها ed في الماضي، بل تتغيّر كلمتها كلّها. مثلاً: get تصبح got، وwear تصبح wore، وmake تصبح made، وgo تصبح went. يجب أن نحفظ هذه الأفعال.
examples: I got a present from my aunt.
My sister wore a pink dress.
My mum made a big cake for Eid.

words.ex: We went to the desert last winter.
The beach was beautiful.

dialogue.t: Where did you go last holiday?
We went to the desert by car.
Wow! Who went with you?
My mum, my dad and my sister went with me.
What did you see?
We saw camels and a lot of stars. It was beautiful!
Was it hot?
Yes, it was hot in the day, but it was cold at night.

grammar.title: Went to ... by ...
grammar.ar: الفعل went هو الماضي من go ومعناه ذهبَ. نستخدم to قبل المكان، ونستخدم by قبل وسيلة النقل بدون the، مثل by car وby bus وby plane. والفعل saw هو الماضي من see ومعناه رأى.
examples: We went to the beach by bus.
My uncle went to Cairo by plane.
We saw a lot of fish in the sea.

words.ex: Let's have a party on Thursday!
Shall we invite our cousins?
I can bring some biscuits.
We have ten guests at the party.
What games do you want to play?
We need some orange juice.

dialogue.t: Let's have a class party on Thursday!
Good idea! We need some juice and cake.
I can bring the cake. What do you want to bring?
I can bring juice and cups. Shall we invite Miss Sara?
Yes! Let's invite our teacher. What games do you want to play?
Let's play musical chairs!
Great! I love musical chairs!

grammar.title: Making Suggestions: Let's and Shall we
grammar.ar: نستخدم Let's مع الفعل في أصله لنقترح شيئاً نفعله معاً، مثل Let's play. ونستخدم Shall we...? لنسأل صديقنا عن اقتراح. ونقول I can bring عندما نريد أن نتطوّع لإحضار شيء، ونستخدم We need some لنقول ما نحتاجه.
examples: Let's make a big cake!
Shall we invite our grandparents?
We need some balloons. I can bring them.

words.ex: My best day was at the zoo.
I liked it because the animals were funny.

Who were you with?
I was with my family and my friends. We ate cake and then we played games.
What did you like?
I liked the games because they were funny.
Why was it the best day?
It was the best day because everyone was happy!

grammar.title: Giving Reasons with Because
grammar.ar: نستخدم because لنذكر السبب، ونضعها في وسط الجملة. نجيب بها عن السؤال Why? الذي معناه لماذا. وكلمة the best تعني الأفضل، ونستخدمها لشيء واحد هو الأحسن من كلّ الأشياء.
examples: I liked the trip because we saw dolphins.
It was the best day because my cousins came.
My best day was at the beach with my family.

words.ex: There are many children in the park.
The girl is sitting on the swing.
Two boys are going down the slide.
The boy is flying a kite.
The old man is feeding the birds.

words.ar: نزهة مع طعام في الهواء الطلق
words.ex: The family is having a picnic under a tree.

dialogue.t: Look at my picture. The boy is flying a kite.
In my picture, he is riding a bike, not flying a kite!
OK! What is the man doing in your picture?
He is feeding the birds.
In my picture, he is reading a book, not feeding the birds.
Another difference! Two girls are playing on the swings.
Yes, two girls are playing on the swings in my picture too.
Great! Let's find more differences.

grammar.title: Present Continuous: am / is / are + -ing
grammar.ar: نستخدم المضارع المستمر للحديث عن شيء يحدث الآن أمامنا. نكوّنه من am أو is أو are ثم الفعل مضافاً إليه ing. مع المفرد نستخدم is، ومع الجمع نستخدم are. انتبه: في العربية نقول «الولد يجري» بدون فعل «يكون»، لكن في الإنجليزية يجب أن نقول The boy is running وليس The boy running.
examples: The boy is flying a kite.
Two girls are playing on the swings.
What is the man doing?

words.ex: What are you doing right now?

words.ar: ابن أو ابنة العم أو الخال
words.ex: My cousin lives in Jeddah.
My mum is in the kitchen.
My dad is cooking rice.
The baby is sleeping now.
My brothers are watching TV.

dialogue.t: Hi, Faisal! What are you doing right now?
Hi, Omar! I'm doing my homework. And you?
I'm talking to you, of course! My dad is cooking in the kitchen.
Cool! My mum is reading a book in the living room.
Where are your sisters? Are they watching TV?
No, they aren't. They're sleeping!
My grandma is sleeping too.
Shh! Let's talk quietly, then.

grammar.title: Present Continuous Questions
grammar.ar: لنسأل سؤالاً جوابه نعم أو لا، نضع am أو is أو are في بداية الجملة قبل الشخص: Are they playing? ونجيب بـ Yes, they are أو No, they aren't. وإذا استخدمنا كلمة سؤال مثل What أو Where نضعها في أول الجملة: What are you doing?
examples: What are you doing right now?
Are they watching TV? No, they aren't.
Is your dad cooking? Yes, he is.

words.ex: What's the weather like in Riyadh?
It's very hot in Riyadh today.
It's sunny, so I'm wearing a cap.
It's windy in Jeddah today.
It's rainy in Abha.
It's cloudy in Tabuk this morning.

dialogue.t: Good morning! What's the weather like in Riyadh?
It's hot and sunny in Riyadh. People are swimming because it's hot.
What's the weather like in Abha?
It's rainy in Abha. People are carrying umbrellas because it's rainy.
And what's the weather like in Jeddah?
It's windy in Jeddah. Children are flying kites because it's windy.
Thank you! And in Tabuk?
It's cold and cloudy in Tabuk. People are wearing jackets because it's cold.

grammar.title: It's + weather / because
grammar.ar: نسأل عن الطقس بـ What's the weather like in...? ونجيب بـ It's ثم صفة الطقس مثل hot أو rainy. لا تنسَ كلمة It، فنقول It's hot وليس Is hot. ونستخدم because بمعنى «لأنّ» لنذكر سبب ما يفعله الناس.
examples: What's the weather like in Dammam?
It's sunny in Riyadh.
People are swimming because it's hot.

words.ex: It's cold, so I need a jacket.
She's wearing a pink scarf.
I'm wearing a green T-shirt today.
He's wearing black boots.
My sister is wearing a new dress for the party.
It's sunny, so I'm wearing a cap.

dialogue.t: Look at the party picture. She's wearing a blue dress and white shoes.
Is she wearing a scarf?
Yes, she is. She's wearing a pink scarf.
Is it Lina? Yes! My turn. He's wearing a black jacket and a red cap.
Is he wearing boots?
Yes, he is. It's cold, so he needs a jacket and boots.
Is it your brother, Ali?
Yes, it is! And I'm wearing a T-shirt today because it's hot.

grammar.title: Wearing / so
grammar.ar: نستخدم is wearing أو am wearing للحديث عن الملابس التي يلبسها شخص الآن. نضع a قبل الاسم المفرد مثل a jacket، ولا نضعها قبل الجمع مثل boots. ونستخدم so بمعنى «لذلك» لنذكر النتيجة: الجو بارد، لذلك أحتاج جاكيت.
examples: She's wearing a dress and a scarf.
It's cold, so I need a jacket.
Is he wearing boots? Yes, he is.

words.ex: The race is starting now!
Our team is winning!
The red team is very good.
Ahmed is passing the ball to Saad.
The boys are jumping very high.
Khalid is running very fast!

dialogue.t: Welcome to Sports Day! Look, the race is starting!
Khalid is running very fast!
Who is winning now?
Yousef is winning! No, wait! Khalid is winning!
Now it's football. Ahmed is passing the ball to Saad.
Saad is kicking the ball... Goal!
The red team is winning! They're jumping and shouting!
What a great Sports Day!

grammar.title: Live commentary: is / are + -ing
grammar.ar: المعلّق الرياضي يستخدم المضارع المستمر لأن الأحداث تحدث أمامه الآن. نضع very قبل الكلمة لتقوية المعنى، مثل very fast أي «سريع جداً». ونسأل عن الشخص الذي يقوم بالفعل بـ Who is ...ing? ونستخدم is دائماً بعد Who.
examples: He's running very fast!
Who is winning now?
She's passing the ball to her friend.

words.ex: I usually walk to school.
We always visit Grandma on Fridays.
Today I'm staying at home.
My dad drinks coffee every day.
He usually plays football, but today he's swimming.
I always play football on Fridays.

dialogue.t: Hi, Salem! Why are you staying at home today?
Because I'm sick. I usually go to the park, but today I'm resting.
Oh no! I always play football on Fridays, but now I'm visiting you!
Thank you! My mum usually works in the morning, but today she's helping me.
What is your brother doing?
He usually plays video games, but today he's reading a story to me.
That's nice! Get well soon.
Thanks, Omar!

grammar.title: Every day vs. Right now
grammar.ar: نستخدم المضارع البسيط مثل play وplays للعادات التي تتكرر، ومعه كلمات مثل usually وalways وevery day. ونستخدم المضارع المستمر am/is/are + ing لما يحدث الآن أو اليوم فقط. مع he وshe نضيف s للفعل في المضارع البسيط: He usually plays. ونربط بين الجملتين بكلمة but.
examples: He usually walks to school, but today he's going by car.
I always play football on Fridays, but now I'm doing my homework.
Why are you wearing a jacket today?

units.cando: Can describe their daily routine and ask others about theirs using simple present tense sentences with times and frequency words.
lessons: Morning Moves
Tell a partner what you do from waking up to arriving at school, then compare routines.
Patterns: I get up at ... o'clock. / Then I ... / What time do you ...? / I ... before/after breakfast.
School Day Schedule
Explain your school timetable to a new online friend and ask about their favourite lesson.
Patterns: On Sunday I have ... / My favourite subject is ... because it's ... / Do you have ... on ...? / Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
How Often?
Do a quick interview about healthy habits and report the answers back.
Patterns: I always/usually/sometimes/never ... / How often do you ...? / He/She ... every day.
After-School Time
Plan a balanced afternoon with a partner: homework, sport, family time and screen time.
Patterns: After school I ... / First I ..., then I ... / I like/don't like ...ing. / Can you ... after school?
Family Helpers
Talk about which jobs each family member does at home and offer to help.
Patterns: My brother/sister ... / Who ... in your house? / I help my mum/dad with ... / Can I help you with ...?
A Day in the Life
Present a short 'day in my life' talk and answer two follow-up questions from the teacher.
Patterns: In the morning/afternoon/evening I ... / At the weekend I ... / I think my day is ... because ...

units.cando: Can describe places in their town, say where things are and ask for and give simple directions.
lessons: What's in My Town?
Describe your neighbourhood to a visitor and find out what their town has.
Patterns: There is a ... near my house. / There are some/lots of ... / Is there a ... in your town? / There isn't a ...
Where Is It?
Use a map to find buildings and explain their location to a partner.
Patterns: The ... is next to/opposite/between/behind the ... / Where is the ...? / It's on ... Street.
Finding the Way
Help a lost tourist get from the mall to the park using simple directions.
Patterns: Go straight on. / Turn left/right at the ... / It's on your left/right. / Excuse me, how do I get to the ...?
At the Shop
Role-play buying things for a school project at a stationery shop.
Patterns: Can I have ..., please? / How much is/are ...? / It's ... riyals. / Have you got any ...?
Getting Around
Talk about how you and your family travel to different places and why.
Patterns: I go to ... by car/bus/metro. / I walk to ... / How do you get to ...? / It's quick/far/near.
My Perfect Street
Design and present an ideal street for kids, then vote on the best ideas together.
Patterns: In my street there is/are ... / You can ... there. / I want a ... because ... / It's got a ...

units.cando: Can describe what people are doing at the moment and talk about the weather and clothes using simple present continuous sentences.
lessons: Picture Story
Describe a busy park picture and find differences with a partner's picture.
Patterns: The boy is ...ing. / Two girls are ...ing. / What is the man doing? / In my picture, he is ...ing, not ...ing.
Video Call Check-In
Call a cousin in another city and tell each other what everyone at home is doing now.
Patterns: My dad is ...ing in the kitchen. / What are you doing right now? / I'm ...ing. / Are they ...ing?
Weather Report
Give a short weather report for Saudi cities and say what people are doing because of the weather.
Patterns: It's hot/sunny/windy/rainy in ... / People are ...ing because it's ... / What's the weather like in ...?
What Are You Wearing?
Describe outfits for different weather and events, and guess who a partner is describing.
Patterns: She's wearing a ... and ... / I'm wearing ... today. / It's cold, so I need a ... / Is he wearing ...?
Sports Day Live
Act as a sports commentator describing a school sports day as it happens.
Patterns: He's running very fast! / They're winning! / Who is ...ing now? / She's ...ing the ball to ...
Now vs. Every Day
Compare what someone usually does with what they are doing today, and explain the difference.
Patterns: He usually ..., but today he's ...ing. / I always ... on Fridays, but now I'm ...ing. / Why are you ...ing today?

units.cando: Can talk about past weekends and special occasions such as Eid using was/were and common past simple verbs, and ask simple questions about the past.
lessons: Where Were You?
Ask a partner where they were at different times last weekend and how it was.
Patterns: I was at ... on Friday. / Where were you on ...? / It was fun/boring/great. / We were at ...
My Weekend
Tell the story of your last weekend in three or four sentences using time words.
Patterns: On Saturday I played/visited/watched ... / First ..., then ..., after that ... / Did you ...? / Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.
Eid Memories
Share how your family celebrated the last Eid and compare celebrations with a partner.
Patterns: We visited my grandparents. / I got a present from ... / I wore ... / What did you do at Eid?
Family Trip
Describe a trip to the desert, the beach or another city, and answer questions about it.
Patterns: We went to ... by ... / It was hot/beautiful/exciting. / We saw ... / Who went with you?
Party Planning
Plan a family gathering or class celebration together: food, games and guests.
Patterns: Let's ... / We need some ... / Shall we invite ...? / I can bring ... / What do you want to ...?
Best Day Ever
Give a short talk about your best day this year and answer the teacher's follow-up questions.
Patterns: My best day was ... / I was with ... / We ... and then we ... / I liked it because ... / It was the best day because ...
